news.title: GreenLight Metals triples Bend project footprint, targets maiden resource in 2027
news.summary:
GreenLight Metals CEO Matt Filgate joined Steve Darling from Proactive to discuss the company's copper-gold exploration activities in Wisconsin, highlighting recent drilling success at its Bend Project, plans to expand the known mineralized footprint and exploration priorities for 2027.

Filgate explained that GreenLight Metals is focused on discovering and advancing volcanogenic massive sulphide (VMS) deposits in Wisconsin, using modern exploration techniques to build on the region's established history of mineral exploration.

At the Bend Project, the company has completed approximately 8,000 metres of drilling, expanding the known strike length of the deposit from approximately 330 metres to between 830 and 850 metres.
Filgate described the progress as "essentially tripling the footprint of that known deposit," highlighting the potential emerging from the company's ongoing exploration program.

Recent results from drillholes B-26-015 and B-26-016 have provided further encouragement, with both holes intersecting substantial massive sulphide mineralization along the eastern extension of the deposit.
Hole B-26-015 returned approximately 25 metres grading 1.3% copper and 1.3 grams per tonne gold, while B-26-016 intersected approximately 30 metres of massive sulphide mineralization with comparable grades.

The results support the company's interpretation that the mineralized system continues beyond previously established boundaries and provide additional targets for follow-up drilling.

Looking ahead, GreenLight Metals is planning approximately 15,000 metres of drilling in 2027, with the potential to expand the program depending on exploration results and priorities.

The planned work will focus on testing further extensions of the Bend deposit, investigating additional geophysical anomalies and conducting infill drilling to improve the geological understanding of the mineralized zones.

The company is targeting a maiden mineral resource estimate around the third quarter of 2027, with an internal target of 15 million to 20 million tonnes. This represents a company objective rather than an established resource.

Beyond Bend, GreenLight Metals is advancing its early-stage Lobo and Lobo East projects, which provide additional opportunities to explore for copper-gold mineralization across its Wisconsin portfolio.

Filgate also discussed the state's mining legislation, the company's engagement with local communities and the potential next steps toward evaluating the economic prospects of the Bend Project.

news.title: Tesla to invest 3 bn euros to expand German factory
news.summary:
US electric carmaker Tesla said Monday it will invest three billion euros ($3.4 billion) to expand its German factory, which will in future have capacity to produce one million driverless Cybercabs annually. 
- 'Enormous significance' -
 
Under the investment plans announced Monday, a new facility will be constructed where up to one million Cybercabs a year will eventually be produced, according to Tesla.
